chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Stepfather's trade and why the family broke up
summary: His stepfather was a shoe cobbler; he and Gus's mother separated, and she moved to Houston for better prospects.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, listen, Gus, what did your step-father do?
No, shoe cobbler. He Fixed shoes.
So is this -- so he could do better in Houston, was that it?
We moved because they separated, too.
And they didn't have any children.
You didn't have any half-brothers or anything.
The only half-sister I have is in Kansas City now. That's my father's side, which is step --
No, I see, yeah. So it's a connection, really, rather than a blood relative.
Well, listen, so your mother got up and went to Houston. Your stepfather remained in Beaumont or something.
I see. And your mother thought she'd do better if she went into a bigger city?
Yeah. That was good. So you and she -- you had to be close, didn't you?
